Nora — thanks for the clear list. High-level summary in-line, full worksheet attached (horizon-econ-sheet-v3.xlsx). TL;DR: with conservative batching and prefix KVCaching we estimate ~35-45% reduction in per-token billable compute vs naive single-request throughput for your workload profile.

Pilot construct (6 months):
- Baseline: hosted pay-as-you-go for mixed 7B/13B usage (no reserved capacity).
- Pilot bundle: 3 months of 25% committed capacity + 3 months burstable credits (~$Xk credit) to cover onboarding spikes. Credits apply first to hosted usage.
- Ops add-on: optional dedicated KV cache for session-heavy endpoints (recommended for Horizon conversational flows).

Quantization guidance:
- 7B: int8 + activation-aware calibration -> minimal measurable quality loss on classification/generation; recommended for high-throughput endpoints.
- 13B: q4f16 or dynamic int8 for balanced latency/cost; offer a 1–2% top-level metric uplift test to measure.

Operational notes on KV caching: prefix cache is safe for pinned models; eviction and TTL policies must be tuned — suggest 24–72h window for Horizon’s usage patterns. We'll include recommended defaults in the sheet.

I'll loop Camila for a short note on implementation effort and Marissa on commercial concessions.

Vivek
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachments: horizon-econ-sheet-v3.xlsx (spreadsheet), redwood-quant-comparison.pdf (benchmark pdf)

Subject: Fwd: Horizon ask — implementation/ops estimate

Vivek / Marissa — forwarding Nora's asks. Quick internal notes:

- Engineering effort: enabling per-route KV cache + monitoring in Dedicated pool ~ 2 sprints (SE time + infra config). We'll need one integration day with Horizon engineering for session id mapping.
- Quantization rollout: for 7B int8 it's low-risk; 13B dynamic quantization requires a validation pass (3–5 eval prompts). Plan: A/B for 2 weeks, keep both variants behind traffic split.
- Risk: for high-safety generative endpoints, auto-quantization could slightly affect prompt sensitivity — recommend including a small quality SLA window in the contract.

Asked product for a short playbook to hand Horizon (I'll draft).

Camila
Solutions Engineering

Subject: Re: Horizon ask — commercial stance and concessions

Team — suggested commercial approach for pilot negotiation:

1) Pilot price structure: 50% of forecasted committed spend paid up-front as a pilot deposit (applied to invoices), remaining billed monthly. This keeps skin in the game for both sides.
2) Credits: offer $30k onboarding credit that phases out after month 3, usable against hosting and monitoring overages.
3) Quantization/Quality concession: include a one-time technical credit (equivalent to ~5% of pilot ARR) if post-quantization A/B tests show model regression beyond agreed thresholds.

Horizon asks on discount bands: they asked verbally for a deeper discount if they commit to a 12-month reserved band post-pilot. Recommend conditional discount schedule: 10% for 12-month commit, 15% for 24-month commit + data-sharing agreement for usage patterns (anonymous).

I'll draft the short commercial term sheet to send to Nora. Thoughts?

Marissa
Director, Commercials

Liam — answers inline and attached a one-pager ops checklist.

- Onboarding credit: yes, credit is agnostic to deployment mode and can be applied to Dedicated if you choose to move mid-pilot; we'll note governance to prevent double-dipping.
- Regression protection: propose we use your eval harness (horizon-eval-metrics.xlsx). Threshold: <2% drop in your primary NLG metric (we can use top-1 BLEU/ROUGE or your chosen F1 for retrieval tasks) triggers a one-time technical credit equal to 5% of pilot ARR. We will jointly sign the test plan pre-rollout.
- Discount scope: 10% applies to compute usage for committed models; add-ons (observability retention, premium SLAs) remain at list unless included in a separate bundling concession. If Horizon signs a 24-month commit, we can consider a bundled discount that includes reduced observability rates — will put options in the term sheet.

Attached: horizon-econ-sheet-v3.xlsx (updated), redwood-ops-cache-checklist.pdf (one-pager).
